newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Crude fails to lift gas oil.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Crude fails to lift gas oil.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps edged up slightly at midday on Wednesday despite large overnight crude gains as the market perceived that the two-month long buying spree maybe coming to an end, traders said.
"The market is not picking up from the crude gains. People are a bit nervous that the buying maybe over," one trader said.
May swaps were last quoted at $25.65/$25.80, up 10 cents from Tuesday, with June also seen firmer by a similar margin at $24.65/$24.80, brokers said.
Overnight June Brent crude on the International Petroleum Exchange closed up 34 cents to $18.61 per barrel with June gas oil ending up $2.25 to $168.25 per tonne.
Industry sources said the buying pattern of the traders this week suggest that they may stop buying from Wednesday.
On Tuesday, despite numerous players willing to sell at the traders' buying level, only two 150,000-barrel cargoes were purchased.
One at $26.20 per barrel for end May loading and another at $26.50 for mid-May loading, both on a free-on-board basis.
The traders last Thursday bought a one-day record of 2.44 million barrels, taking their tally to nearly 18 million barrels of diesel since March 3.
But despite the large purchase, physical prices have instead trekked a steady downward path from a high of about $28.75 per barrel to around $26.00 over the past two months.
As a result of the declining prices, the East-West arbitrage has narrowed to $15.75 per tonne, making it uneconomical to ship cargoes over.
Fuel oil swaps firmed slightly with May quoted up 25 cents from Tuesday at $98.50/$99.50, brokers said.
